originalTitle: ITC charts growth strategy as cigarette tax hike hits stock
simplifiedContent: ITC, a company that makes cigarettes among other things, is dealing with a problem caused by the government increasing taxes on cigarettes. To handle this, the company plans to raise the prices of its cigarettes a little at a time, create new products, and sell more of other types of goods it makes. ITC will also spend Rs 20,000 crore over the next five years to grow its business. The company wants to make its other businesses, like food and other everyday items, stronger. It's also thinking about selling shares of its technology business, ITC Infotech, to the public once it's big enough.

originalTitle: US stocks today: US stocks fall as Big Tech earnings rekindle AI spending worries; oil hits $100
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the main US stock markets (like the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq) had a big drop on Thursday. This was mostly because big technology companies like Alphabet and Tesla released their financial reports, and it made investors worried about how much they're spending on artificial intelligence. At the same time, oil prices jumped to $100 a barrel due to tension in the Middle East, which could lead to higher inflation and interest rates. This combination of worries led to a sharp decline in the stock markets. Overall, it's a sign that investors are getting nervous about the direction of the economy.

originalTitle: Brent crude oil price surges past $100 as Houthi tanker attacks in Red Sea rattle markets
simplifiedContent: The price of Brent crude oil has gone up past $100 per barrel. This happened because a group called the Houthi rebels attacked some oil tankers in the Red Sea that belong to Saudi Arabia. This attack is making people worry that there won't be enough oil available, which is why the price is going up. As a result, people are also getting worried about inflation, which is when the prices of things in general start to rise. This is important because it can affect the overall economy and the prices of things we buy.

originalTitle: US stocks tumble on renewed concerns over massive AI spending, rising crude prices
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a rough morning, with major indexes like the S&P 500, Dow Jones, and Nasdaq Composite all losing value. This happened because investors are worried about big companies spending a lot of money on artificial intelligence (AI) and also because crude oil prices are going up. As of 10am, the S&P 500 and Dow Jones were down 1%, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.8%. This matters because when the stock market goes down, it can affect the value of investments that people have in the market. The drop in stock prices is a sign that investors are feeling uncertain and cautious about the current state of the market.

originalTitle: IEX Q1 results: Net profit grows 12% YoY to  ₹135 crore; electricity volumes rise 16%
simplifiedContent: Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) just announced its results for the first quarter of the year, and they're looking good. The company made a net profit of ₹135 crore, which is 12% more than it made during the same time last year. This increase is largely due to a rise in electricity trading - the company traded 15.9% more electricity than it did last year, with a total of 37.5 billion units. This is a positive sign for the company, as it shows that it's doing well and that there's strong demand for electricity. Overall, IEX's strong results suggest that the company is performing well and growing steadily.

originalTitle: Sebi proposes faster online dispute resolution, bigger role for exchanges and depositories
simplifiedContent: The main stock market regulator, Sebi, wants to make it easier and faster for investors to resolve disputes online. They plan to do this by setting stricter time limits and making the process more enforceable. Sebi also wants to change the way arbitration works, which is the process of resolving disputes between investors and companies. This matters because it will help investors get their issues resolved more quickly and efficiently. By making these changes, Sebi aims to improve the overall experience for investors and make the market a fairer place.
